resources.name: 34th Avenue Open Streets Coalition
resources.mission: The 34th Avenue Open Streets Coalition, in partnership with NYC DOT, transforms 26 blocks in Queens, NY into a vibrant, year-round public space. Through diverse programs, events, and cultural activities, we create a welcoming space for neighbors of all ages to connect, learn, and have fun. By collaborating with local organizations and city agencies, we provide essential services and build a stronger, more connected community. We offer an outdoor space for many groups or organizations to meet or perform.

resources.name: NAUW-Flushing North Shore
resources.mission: The National Association of University Women (NAUW) is a community-based women's organization founded in Washington D.C. in 1910. The NAUW's mission is to serve women, youth, and the disadvantaged in our communities and in developing countries by strategically partnering with allied organizations to address educational issues and advance the status of women's issues, specifically in the areas of: 1) Education; 2) Literacy; 3) Scholarship; and 4) National & International Affairs. We have various community service events throughout the year that are open to the public in the Flushing North Shore Area of Queens.

resources.name: Queens World Film Festival
resources.mission: Queens World advances public participation in film screenings by utilizing traditional and alternative screening locations and venues to screen independent cinema. Through the implementation of educational programs, we provide opportunities for individuals to share ideas and develop analog, digital, visual, and performing arts projects. We would love to partner with you to bring our unique programs and screenings to your programs.
resources.languages: English, but we screen films from all over the world in all languages.
resources.fees: There are free programs and screenings, there are some programs that are fee for service and some events are ticketed.

resources.name: The Connected Chef Foundation, Inc.
resources.mission: The Connected Chef works to build community-rooted food distribution that ensures every household has access to local, nutritious food on a weekly basis. Our vision is a community-controlled food system that provides fresh, local ingredients; healthy eating education; and pathways to financial agency. Through our programming, the Connected Chef delivers fresh, nutrient dense, culturally appropriate groceries to underserved and under-resourced communities in New York City, while creating job opportuni - ties and deepening community engagement through food. Our Woodside community food hub provides fresh weekly groceries, farm stand, and workshops and classes that offer wrap-around services based on community member needs. Kim Calichio, Co-founder and Executive Director, can be reached at kim@theconnectedchef.org.
resources.fees: Yes, we offer a sliding-scale grocery program with 60% of clients receiving free groceries.

resources.name: Together We Can/Family Youth Peer Support Services
resources.mission: Mission: Empowering Queens residents by linking them to Youth and Family Support, Educational Opportunities, Fresh Food Resources, and other Community Services. We create culturally sensitive programs that increase resources needed by our multi-ethnic families residing in Elmhurst, Corona, and Jackson Heights, Queens. Our eventual goal is the creation of community center which will allow us to greatly expand our services to those in need.
